title: Les bassins hydrographiques du Cameroun
through_line: On remonte un fleuve : d’abord l’eau, puis les régions qu’elle traverse.

blocks.vo_line: L’hydrographie, c’est l’ensemble des cours d’eau d’une région.
blocks.shot: The outline of Cameroon seen from high above, narrow and pointed at the north, wide in the south; many small blue streams drawing themselves across it, morning light.

blocks.vo_line: Un bassin est la région arrosée par un fleuve et ses affluents.
blocks.shot: One wide river in a valley with several smaller rivers joining it from the hills, and a soft tinted area spreading outward to show the land this river waters.

blocks.vo_line: Un affluent se jette dans un fleuve plus grand pour le grossir.
blocks.shot: A narrow river flowing into a much wider river, the two waters meeting, the wide river visibly swelling and continuing thicker than before.

blocks.vo_line: Le Cameroun compte quatre bassins : le Tchad, le Niger, l’Atlantique et le Congo.
blocks.shot: The map of Cameroon with four basins tinted in their real places — Chad at the northern tip, Niger around Garoua, Atlantic across the centre and south, Congo in the far south-east corner — and four arrows showing where the water finally goes.

blocks.vo_line: Le Logone arrose Maroua, et la Bénoué arrose Garoua.
blocks.shot: Split view, both in the real north. Left: the real Sahel of the Far North of Cameroon: flat pale ochre plain, dusty pale sky, sparse flat-topped thorny acacias, rounded granite domes of the Mandara hills, conical earth houses with pointed thatch caps, millet granaries, a humped zebu, with the Logone running north past Maroua. Right: the real Sudanian savannah of the North of Cameroon: tall golden grass, broad scattered trees, a wide river showing pale sandbanks, wooden pirogues at a river landing, with the Bénoué turning west at Garoua.

blocks.vo_line: La Sanaga rejoint l’océan, et la Sangha coule dans la forêt.
blocks.shot: Split view. Left: the real forest of southern Cameroon: dense green rainforest, oil palms, red laterite earth, a wide brown river, the Sanaga widening towards the Atlantic with mangroves and the dark cone of Mount Cameroon on the horizon. Right: the real equatorial forest of eastern Cameroon: very dense dark forest, very tall emergent trees, slow still black water under deep shade, the Sangha flowing slowly under the trees.
